The weakest part is that the external drive will be the only copy of your photos once you wipe the laptop. A checksum proves the copy matched the original at that moment, but it can't protect you if the drive fails, gets lost, or is knocked off a desk next week. Family photos are irreplaceable, and a single drive is a common point of failure.

The fix is cheap: before wiping, make a second copy somewhere else, such as a cloud service or a second drive kept in a different place. Then you have the original-equivalent plus a backup, instead of one copy and a hope.

Two smaller things worth checking:

1. **Are the photos really all on the laptop?** Confirm you've covered every location: Pictures folder, Desktop, Downloads, photo-app libraries (which can hide files in their own formats), and any cloud-synced folders that might only be stubs and not real local files.

2. **Does the checksum cover what you think it does?** Make sure it compares the source files to the copies file by file, and that the count matches 3,112. Also open a handful of photos from the drive to check they actually look right.

The tight timeline also leaves no room to discover a problem: wiping Saturday morning means any issue found Saturday afternoon is unfixable. I'd leave the wipe until you've had a day with the backup in place, if the buyer's noon handoff allows it. If not, the second copy on Friday is the one thing I wouldn't skip.
